text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Shop owners, concerned over growing shoplifting, plan to set up association to combat problem through increased security and prosecutions.

- Libya pays off some debts to Maltese companies. Foreign Minister George Vella told Parliament that following talks between the two countries, Libya had started paying off debts to Maltese companies. He did not say how much has been paid or to which company.

- Nationalist Party sues Broadcasting Authority and Public Broadcasting Services. The opposition party seeks redress over the transmission by state-owned television station of meetings by Prime Minister Alfred Sant with the self-employed on new system of indirect taxes to replace VAT. The party accuses station of bias and says it should also transmit meetings which opposition leader Eddie Fenech Adami is having with the self-employed.
- Engineer seriously hurt in freak incident. The man was working on a ladder placed on top of a van when the van was hit by a truck, toppling the ladder.
